newsitem.title: UK: Gold tumbles to near 2-year lows.
newsitem.headline: Gold tumbles to near 2-year lows.

text.p: The price of gold dropped to its lowest level in nearly two years on Thursday after heavy and protracted selling from mining companies and speculators cracked a key support level.
"Why it's held up under so much selling pressure is the mystery," said analyst Andy Smith of Union Bank of Switzerland.
Bullion fixed at $377.00 an ounce in the afternoon, the lowest fixing since March 6, 1995, and then headed still lower to test the waters at below $376 an ounce.
Prices had been edging closer to a key technical support level at around $377 an ounce in recent days.
But a drop below that chart point triggered a flurry of selling based on computer-generated models, sending gold spiralling to a low bid of $375.70 an ounce.
Technical analysts, who study historical price charts to forecast future movements, said gold was now vulnerable to further drops, potentially to $370 an ounce.
"Three successive days of European closes below $376.87 will target $369.50," said Brian Marber, an independent technical analyst. But he cautioned that gold may yet bounce up.
"Gold has in the past ended a bear market with a false move into lower regions," Marber siad.
Prices have been locked in a steady downtrend since rallying to a high of $418 an ounce in February this year, hurt by a dearth of interest from investors who prefer to play in surging stock markets.
Cash-rich investment funds, most of them U.S.-based, have been building up speculative "short" positions in the market in anticipation that prices will head south.
But gold had moved briskly higher last week after speculators decided the price of gold had bottomed out. However, a flood of selling from gold producers reversed the trend.
Next week's Thanksgiving holiday in the United States and upcoming expiry of over-the-counter options likely provided additional impetus to the market to move lower, Smith said.
"Perhaps there was a keenness in the market to stabilise at a new level so the U.S. could have its holiday in peace," he said. "It may have been a clear the decks move."

The two biggest producers of the metal, Australia and South Africa, also both faced a bounce in their domestic currencies overnight, which may have encouraged miners to sell more gold forward, Smith added.
Miners typically lock in favourable prices for yet-unmined output by selling gold borrowed from central banks. They then pay back the banks after mining and refining their own gold.
"I'm not saying that's the main reason for today's price movement, but it follows steady, inexorable selling from many many sources," Smith said.
Fundamentally, gold remains weak, and desite the seasonal peak for demand, the jewellery industry has been holding off in hopes of cheaper gold price.

World demand for slipped two percent in the third quart4er of 1996 to 654.8 tonnes, whilc demand year-to-date is down four percent at 1,5666 tonnes compared to last year, the World Gold Council said this week.

Silver prices headed lower in sympathy with gold, losing nine cents from Wednesday's London close. But it remained in its recent price range at $4.86/$4.88 an ounce. Platinum and palladium were slightly weaker.
--Lida Poletz, London newsroom +44 171 542 2936
